messages:
sara_support: FYI — new signup CobaltHealth. Console shows API key created but their requests get 403. Can someone triage?

mike_cust: Hi, Sara. We tried curl from our app and getting 403 Forbidden every time. Key visible in console UI. Extremely high priority for onboarding today.

ali_engineer: Can you paste the curl and response? Also which project/org is the key shown under?

mike_cust: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-cobalt-ABCD1234\" 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"hi"}'

Response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":{"code":403,"message":"Caller does not have permission to use model: redwood-1"}}

Key appears under org: CobaltHealth (org-id: org-9987), project: default (project-id: proj-9987). We left SSO flow and confirm onboarding completed.

sara_support: We verified console shows key id = key-0a1b2c3. No obvious TTL. No billing issues on their account. Repro steps attached in the ticket #INC-10234.

provisioner_bot: [automated] provisioner.create_key key=key-0a1b2c3 status=created project=proj-9987 role_bindings=[] timestamp=2025-07-15T14:10:22Z

ali_engineer: role_bindings=[] is the smoking gun — key created but no IAM roles attached. That explains 403. How did provisioner skip binding? Any recent deploys to provisioner-service?

jess_eng_iam: I'm on it. Checking provisioner logs for that run. @ali_engineer do we have a fallback that retries role binding?

ali_engineer: There is a retry but it only runs on network errors. If the binding step returned success but upstream IAM accepted an empty policy, it might have been a logic bug. Need logs.

jess_eng_iam: Found log snippet: \n```
2025-07-15T14:10:20Z provisioner: create_key start key=key-0a1b2c3
2025-07-15T14:10:21Z provisioner: bind_role attempt=1 key=key-0a1b2c3 -> iam-api: 200 OK, response={"bindings":null}
2025-07-15T14:10:21Z provisioner: bind_role result=success key=key-0a1b2c3
```\nLooks like IAM returned a 200 with a null bindings payload and provisioner treats that as success. Bug.

mike_cust: Is there a workaround we can do on our side? We need a working key ASAP.

jess_eng_iam: Temporary workaround: we can manually attach the correct role to key-0a1b2c3 via internal admin API. I can run it now with your consent. It will give model.use permission for redwood-1.

mike_cust: Please do. Confirmed.

jess_eng_iam: Running: \nPOST /internal/admin/v1/keys/key-0a1b2c3/roles \nBody: {"roles":["models.use:redwood-1"]} \n
provisioner_bot: [automated] admin.bind_roles key=key-0a1b2c3 roles=[models.use:redwood-1] result=ok timestamp=2025-07-15T14:17:05Z

mike_cust: Retried curl — now 200 OK. Thank you!

ali_engineer: Root cause: provisioner accepted null bindings from IAM as success. Create a quick patch to validate response payload and retry on null. I'll push a hotfix and restart the job.

jess_eng_iam: Patch ready: check for response.bindings !== null && length > 0. If not, treat as error and retry 3x with backoff. Also adding an alert for bind_role returning 200 with empty payload.

sara_support: Thanks everyone. I'll update the customer that a manual bind fixed it and an engineering hotfix is rolling out.

mike_cust: Appreciated. Please send a note when the permanent fix is live so we can remove the temporary monitoring we added.

ali_engineer: Noted — assigning to eng-iam for follow-up and postmortem. Patch will be deployed in next 20min. Will follow up here with deploy status. :thumbsup:

provisioner_bot: [automated] deploy provisioner v1.4.7-hotfix start timestamp=2025-07-15T14:22:00Z

ali_engineer: Deploy completed, smoke tests passed. Added metric to track empty-bind responses.

sara_support: Closing loop with customer, marking incident resolved in ticket. Thanks all. :tada:
